books.name: Bĕreʾshith
books.line: From the creation of the world to one chosen family, ending in Miṣrayim
books.intro: The book narrows from all of humanity to one family. Two parashiyyoth cover twenty generations; ten cover four. Axis event: Lekh Lĕkha (Genesis 12:1), where the story turns from the world to ʾAvraham.

books.name: Shĕmoth
books.line: The family becomes a people: freed from Miṣrayim, entering the covenant at Sinai, given the Mishkan
books.intro: The book moves in three steps: out of Miṣrayim, up to Sinai, and Hashem's Presence coming down into the Mishkan. Axis event: the covenant at Sinai (Yithro and Mishpaṭim, Exodus 19 to 24), proposed and freely accepted. It is what the Exodus was for: "you will serve God on this mountain" (3:12).

The Calf comes forty days after Sinai, a lesson in how quickly people fall back on worship of their own making.

books.name: Wayyiqraʾ
books.line: How the people can live near Hashem: qorbanoth, ṭumʾa and ṭahŏra, and qĕdhushsha of people, time and Land
books.intro: The whole book is spoken from the Mishkan at Sinai. It asks how a people can live near Hashem, and it widens outward: the altar, the body, the people, time, the Land. Its key word is qĕdhushsha (being set apart for Hashem). Axis event: Nadhav and ʾĂvihuʾ die on the Mishkan's first day (Shĕmini, Leviticus 10). Moshe answers with "through those near to Me I will be set apart" (10:3), and the Talmud (Qiddushin 30a) places the middle word of the Torah a few verses later, at 10:16.

books.name: Bĕmidhbar
books.line: From Sinai to the edge of the Land; the first generation fails, the second arrives
books.intro: The book is organized by place, and it opens and closes with a census: the generation that left Miṣrayim (Numbers 1) and the generation that will enter the Land (Numbers 26). Axis event: the spies (Shĕlaḥ Lĕkha, Numbers 13 to 14), which turn an eleven-day trip into forty years. The 38 years of wandering fall silently between Qoraḥ and Ḥuqqath.

books.name: Dĕvarim
books.line: Moshe restates the Torah (Mishne Torah) on the plains of Moʾav and the covenant is completed there: look back, the miṣwoth, the covenant, his death
books.intro: Tradition calls this book Mishne Torah, the Torah restated (Deuteronomy 17:18). Moshe restates it on the plains of Moʾav in his last weeks, and there the people enter the covenant a second time, completing the pact made at Sinai. It follows his speeches: look back, lay the foundations, teach the laws, seal the covenant, hand over. Axis event: the covenant in Moʾav (Ki Thavoʾ and Niṣṣavim, Deuteronomy 28:69–29:14), made with those standing there and those not yet born.

spine.intro: One idea ties the books together: Sinai sits in the middle. From Exodus 19 to Numbers 10:10 the people stay at the mountain for about a year, and that year fills roughly a third of the Torah. Everything before it moves toward Sinai; everything after it moves from Sinai toward the Land. The Sinai year starts in the middle of Shĕmoth and ends early in Bĕmidhbar, so no book boundary matches a period boundary.

covenant.intro: Following José Faur's Understanding the Covenant, the hooks name every place a covenant is made, remembered, broken or renewed, so the thread runs through all five books. The pact is made at Sinai and completed in Moʾav, which is why both ends of the spine matter.
